events.text: A young fighter has been watching you train from the fence for a month. Today {npc} climbs over it, kneels, and asks you to teach {him} everything you know.

effects.log: {npc} is clumsy, stubborn, and up before you every morning. You find that you have a great deal to teach.

choices.text: Tell {him} to find a better teacher

effects.log: {He} goes, and comes back a month later, and climbs the fence again. You give up and start teaching.

events.text: {npc}, your student, wins a great tournament, using a form you invented and never finished. {He} bows to you from the ring, in front of everyone.

effects.log: Your art will outlive you now. The murim calls it by {his} name, and {he} corrects them every time: it is yours.
{He} sees anyway. {He} finds you on the road home and walks the rest of it with you.

events.text: You realise one winter that everything you know about the martial way exists only in your body, and your body will not last forever. You buy ink, and a great deal of paper.

choices.text: Write it down honestly, mistakes and all

effects.log: The first page takes a month. You write about the things you got wrong. They turn out to be the useful part.

choices.text: Write down only the best of it

effects.log: Clean forms, clean lessons. It reads beautifully. Something is missing, and you will find out what.

events.text: The book is finished: three volumes, drawings in your own hand. A sect wants to buy it. A village school wants to borrow it. A young stranger wants to copy it.

effects.log: It is copied in three provinces within ten years. Your art becomes something people learn from strangers, which is how arts survive.

choices.text: Give it to the village school

effects.log: The children learn from it badly and enthusiastically. One of them, twenty years later, learns it well.

events.text: A child is asleep on your doorstep in the snow, with a note pinned to the coat: please. {npc} wakes, looks at you, and does not cry, which is worse.

mem.note: took me in from the snow

effects.log: A bowl of rice, a blanket, a name for the register. You did not plan on this. Plans are overrated.

choices.text: Find the child a good family

effects.log: A kind family in the next village. {npc} visits you every new year, without fail, for the rest of your life.

events.text: {npc}, the child from the snow, is grown, and comes to tell you {he} has a shop of {his} own now, a small one, and has turned out well. {He} brings the note from the coat. It still says please.

effects.log: {He} holds your hands a long time. Somewhere out in the world now is a whole life that exists because you opened the door.
Your old coat, the one that is warm and is not what it was. {He} keeps it until {he} is old too, and then gives it to someone in the snow.

events.text: The village has no school. The children run wild, and the old schoolmaster died last winter. The headman looks at you, because you can read, and write, and hit things.

effects.log: Twelve children, a barn, a stack of borrowed books, and martial arts in the afternoon, which is the only reason half of them come.

choices.text: Find a teacher and pay for it

effects.log: A young scholar who failed the exams and is glad of the work. You visit every month to teach the afternoon class.

events.text: The school has run for years. One of its first students comes back as a magistrate, another as a physician, a third as a famous fighter. They all come back on the same day, which is not an accident.

choices.text: Ring the school bell for them

effects.log: They have a feast in the barn. Someone makes a speech. You hide behind the rice wine.

choices.text: Make them teach a class each

effects.log: The children are delighted. The magistrate is a terrible teacher. The fighter is a wonderful one.

events.text: Every spring the river takes someone at the ford. This spring it was a child. You stand at the water and decide that it will not happen again.

effects.log: Stone by stone, between the seasons. People laugh, then help.

choices.text: Raise the money for a bridge

effects.log: You shame every merchant in the province into giving something. Masons arrive in the summer.

events.text: The bridge is finished, and the village wants to name it after you. Nobody has drowned at the ford since it was built.

effects.log: Your name on a bridge. People will walk over it every day for three hundred years, and most of them will not know who you were. That is the right amount of fame.
The child's name on the bridge. The mother comes every morning to touch it.

events.text: You plant a plum tree at your gate, knowing you will not see it at its best. An old neighbour watches and says that is the only kind of tree worth planting.

effects.log: Nine trees along the road. The children help, and argue about which one is theirs.
One tree, watered every morning. It becomes the way you begin the day.

events.text: The plum trees are tall now. In spring the whole road is white with blossom, and strangers stop to sit under them, and young couples meet there.

choices.text: Sit under them with a cup of tea

effects.log: You watch a pair of children climb the tree you planted for them. They will plant their own one day. That is how a place remembers people.

choices.text: Give the trees to the village

effects.log: The village calls the road Plum Blossom Road. Nobody remembers why. The trees remember.
